image.prompt: Use case: historical-scene game prop reference. One isolated sculptural dragon-head figurehead and its short integrated curved mounting neck, built for a Joseon Korean turtle ship. Entire object fully visible with generous margin, three-quarter SIDE view so both length and depth are readable, even studio illumination against a plain uniform light-gray opaque background. Fierce broad eyebrow ridge and forceful blunt snout, open jaw with a clean hollow smoke/cannon aperture, two restrained backswept horns, compact thick carved whisker ridges fused firmly to the muzzle, large angular carved scales and strong Korean guardian-dragon silhouette. Mouth and horns must remain readable at distance. It is a real heavy carved timber naval figurehead with blackened bronze-colored surface, muted old brass patina on a few raised edges, deep carved eye sockets and dark throat, aged matte weathered materials. Grounded cinematic film-prop quality inspired by Korean naval war epics. The neck curves gently upward from a substantial FLAT rear mounting face, not a detached floating head; front points horizontally forward. Bilateral symmetry. Model-ready economical broad forms, no wispy hair or wires, no fine needle teeth, no filigree that would require many polygons. Approximate full shape proportions length5.6,width1.8,height2.7. No ship, water, smoke, fire, pedestal, neighboring objects, human, text, watermark, border, dramatic shadow or cropped part.

rejectionCriteria: mouth fused shut or cannon aperture lost
